changes.text: [UNSTABLE] TPMS 'is a car following me?' detector: 5 tyre-sensor decoders (Ford, Toyota, Hyundai/VDO, Schrader, Schrader-GM), FSK+OOK, runs on one radio. Self-test passes on hardware; NOT yet tested near a real car.
Long transmits no longer trip the watchdog and reboot the Crow (tested on hardware).
ProtoPirate file loading no longer crashes on large/complex .sub files (tested on hardware).
Fast SD format (one pass instead of deleting every file); deep-folder delete fixed.
WiFi stack removed: much more free memory (15 KB -> 51 KB) and flash.
Sleazy Crow: community fork of Senape3000's EvilCrowRF-V2 firmware (based on v1.1.3). Bluetooth name is now SleazyCrow.
Bluetooth no longer drops ~12 s after connecting on Android: incoming commands run on their own task and stable connection parameters are requested.
No boot crash when built with Arduino core 3.3.x (BLE controller memory was freed before NimBLE started).
Toolchain and NimBLE pinned so every build is identical (fixes the 'adc_oneshot.h' compile error).
File uploads: a full queue no longer drops chunks, and missing/out-of-order chunks fail with an error instead of saving a corrupted file.
ProtoPirate decode results show the protocol type name instead of a number.
Boot log prints the firmware name, version and upstream project.
[UNSTABLE] Opt-in unstable channel (Settings > Updates) with a warning; unstable updates are always labelled and confirmed.
App self-update now works on modern Android (checksum-verified download, system installer). Not yet tested end-to-end on a phone.
TPMS screen: sensors with make, pressure, temperature; sensitivity modes.
Sub-GHz playlists (files + pauses, repeat, gap, loop, save, export to SD, UberGuidoZ playlist import).
Uploads over ~122 KB were silently truncated; large files are now split or refused.
Every tab browsable without a Crow; Play Sub File; ProtoPirate folder browser; clearer connect errors.
Phone-based surveillance/tracker detection removed (phone radios can't reliably see the targets).
Sleazy Crow app: installs alongside the official EvilCrow RF app; updates come from the Sleazy Crow releases.
Flipper Sub-GHz DB: pick which sections to copy to the SD card instead of the whole database; brute-force folders are opt-in.
Optional 'format SD card first' and an explainer before the download.
Large RAW .sub files are split into smaller pieces so they upload reliably (playback is identical).
Uploads no longer report false failures ('Null check operator' race).
Uploads about 40x faster; live time-remaining estimate.
Transmit button toggles continuous transmission on/off.
Brute force: US/EU frequency choice and timing (te) override.
File preview loads only when requested, so opening files is instant.
